literature_comparison.Dietmann–Elsholtz: Published unnumbered theorem on p. 177 and quantitative argument on p. 178. Eventual existence for Gaussian restricted sums, with a lower bound of order at least n^(1-delta) for each delta>0 over unrestricted summand sizes.
literature_comparison.Howe–Huffman–Kohlmeyer–Kruer: Hexagon 2611.00370v1, Theorem 1.1. Gaussian restricted binary existence for all positive n=2 mod 4. The quaternionic norm-counting method is attributed.
literature_comparison.Ramaré–Viswanadham: arXiv:2509.23260v1, introduction and Theorem 1.6. The introduction discusses the split-prime Eisenstein set. The additive theorem concerns three primitive Gaussian values.
literature_comparison.comparison: The checked results supply a Gaussian precedent, a multidimensional correlation, and a sieve conditional on progression remainders. The fixed-target Eisenstein lower bound with moving windows requires the directional shell estimate, all-valuation local reduction, and bounded-multiplicity cofactor argument. The comparison is scoped to these sources. Broader historical priority remains open.
literature_comparison.Loughran–Matthiesen: JEMS 26 (2024), Theorem 1.9. Its independent-linear-parts condition excludes the fixed-total forms t and n−t, also after the mixed residue-class parametrization. Using two independent variables frees the total and gives an average over targets.
literature_comparison.Iwaniec: Acta Arith. 29 (1976), Theorem 1, condition (Omega 2) and the remainder term. The direct exclusion of 0 and n at inert primes has sieve dimension one. Sifting a single form after restricting the other would need progression counts for that restricted sequence, uniform in the target and the translated interval, as well as control of the unsifted tail.
literature_comparison.Greaves: Acta Arith. 29 (1976), unnumbered main theorem in Section 1. For n outside 0, 1, 5 modulo 8 it gives a lower bound of order n/(log n)^(5/2) for prime pairs p,q at most sqrt(n)/2 for which n−p²−q² is a sum of two squares. This supplies the Gaussian argument of Dietmann–Elsholtz. The prime-variable cutoff leaves the division of the remaining two squares unrestricted.

inputs: Voight, Main Theorem 28.5.3 and Propositions 41.3.1 and 41.3.6
Deligne, Theorems 4.9 and 5.1, and Weil I, Theorem 1.6
findings: Class number one gives the projective finite quotient. The order-unit kernel is ±1 at level 3, and the projective stabilizers at the level cosets are trivial. The equal finite orbit measures and the constant from Schur orthogonality yield the same operator norm as coset counting.

Lifting g only at level primes makes it commute with the right-ideal representative supported at m. Principalizing gives the inverse finite argument before conjugation, and averaging over the twelve generators counts each ideal once.

The upper triangular cosets at ell^a have ell^i translates for each diagonal pair. The normalized spherical function cancels the ell^i factor and gives the all-ideal eigenvalue ell^(a/2) times the complete symmetric polynomial in the unitary Satake roots. Deligne bounds both roots by one, uniformly in the weight and level.

A finite-dimensional split local factor kills the norm-one group. Real density excludes it at positive weight. At weight zero strong approximation and quadratic Dirichlet characters composed with reduced norm give exactly the joint signs.
bounded_controls: Independent scalar enumeration on the six fixed level-3 cosets checked degrees, both norm signs, matrix symmetry, prime-power recurrence through m=16 and coprime multiplicativity at m=10.

Separate exact rational arithmetic used the k=1 action on imaginary quaternions by conjugation and two equivariant tests on the 36 elements of the projective level-3 group. It checked equivariance, self-adjointness for m=2,4,5, T_4=T_2^2−2I and T_10=T_2 T_5.
